pairs.difference: A: the console body, floor plates and lever are all neutral steel grey. The only colour is the orange diamond wall and small red/yellow/green buttons, so subject chroma is 0.025, well below the real cards. In the lens the buttons merge into one orange mass and the card reads as grey plus orange, warm share 0.91. B: the popcorn cart has red, cream and gold local colours against a blue diamond background. Its shadows stay red-brown, and it sits inside the real ranges.
pairs.fix: Paint the console body a clear local colour, such as a soft teal or blue painted metal, not bare grey steel. Give the floor a faint cool tint and keep the buttons as distinct red, yellow and green.

pairs.difference: A: the dish tower is one flat pure fire-engine red. In the lens its shaded side stays the same saturated red (shadow chroma 1.49, above the real range). The white dish shifts to cream and the dunes are a single saturated orange-yellow. B: the sandcastle uses related tan-to-brown shadows, with a green bucket and a blue spade as small accents, and stays within range.
pairs.fix: Darken the red tower's shaded side toward a deeper maroon instead of an equally bright red. Keep the dish a cool clean white and soften the sand to a paler beige.

pairs.difference: B: the saturated violet stripe background (chroma 0.25, above every real card) fights the planet. In the lens the planet and ring collapse into one yellow mass with no shadow hue, so it is a two-hue pure-colour card. A: the coral sandals with yellow straps on teal have a darker red-orange shadow side, and every field is in range.
pairs.fix: Calm the purple background to a softer, lighter lilac. Give the planet a darker orange-brown shaded side and a separate ring colour so the planet and ring don't merge into one yellow.

pairs.difference: B: the orange rover body fades in the lens to a dull khaki. The wheels and shadows drop to flat near-black navy and grey (shadow chroma 0.36, the lowest here), on an acid-green burst over a grey ground. A: the yellow taxi on a blue burst keeps warm brown road shadows. Its shadow chroma is also slightly low, but less so.
pairs.fix: Shade the rover's orange body toward a rich burnt orange, not grey-khaki. Give the tyres and ground shadows a cool blue-violet tint instead of flat black-grey.

pairs.difference: A: the yellow submarine sits on a dark, muted bottle-green radial background (chroma 0.095, below every real card, and darker than any anchor background). The yellow hull is the only loud mass, and its shadows go orange-ochre. B: the red-and-silver rocket on a bright cyan burst is a simple palette, but it stays in range. Both are borderline.
pairs.fix: Make the background a brighter, lighter sea green or aqua, like the other cards. Keep the shaded side of the yellow hull a warm golden ochre.

pairs.difference: B: the teal saucer's shaded body becomes a flat dark grey-green in the lens (shadow chroma 0.51, low). The whole card is pulled warm by the saturated golden background (warm share 0.76, above range), and orange bulbs ring the rim. A: the orange player on violet rings is also a strong two-hue card (hue families 1.8), but its shadows keep colour.
pairs.fix: Shade the saucer with a deep rich teal instead of murky grey-green. Cool the background to a paler lemon yellow so the card is less uniformly warm.

pairs.difference: A: in the lens the asteroid is a dull purple-brown with a near-black plum shadow half (shadow chroma 0.60, below range), and the orange flames read as the same brownish mass. B: the scarf is one pure red (subject chroma 0.22, high), but its shadow stays a related deep crimson.
pairs.fix: Paint the rock a warmer, clearer brown-violet with a deep purple, not muddy black, shadow side. Make the flames a distinct bright orange-yellow.

pairs.difference: B: almost the whole card is one lavender-grey hue family: the moon ground, the white habitat and the violet sky. The only other colours are a small blue dome and a yellow door. Warm share is 0.005 and hue families 1.6, both outside the real range. In the lens the shadows are saturated violet (shadow chroma 1.63). A: the tiki bar is busy (7 hue families) but uses natural local colours: thatch brown, green stools, cyan water and fruit.
pairs.fix: Give the moon ground a neutral warm grey-beige instead of lavender. Paint the habitat in off-white with one coloured trim, and keep the shadows a soft blue-grey instead of strong violet.

pairs.difference: A: the telescope tube is cream instead of a neutral white, and the legs and rings are saturated copper-orange. It sits on a grey-blue mound under a pure cyan stripe background, slightly below the real warm-share range. The cream-for-white swap matches the lessons. B: the green binoculars on a yellow wooden floor have near-black shadows (shadow chroma 0.43), which is also low, so this pair is uncertain.
pairs.fix: Paint the telescope tube a clean light grey or white and tone the orange legs toward a natural wood brown. Soften the cyan background.

pairs.difference: A: the bouncy castle is pure yellow and red-orange on a blue burst, with high subject chroma and many hue families. B: the water polo goal is near-monochrome blue, with a white frame and one orange ball, so its warm share is low. Each has one borderline field, and neither departs from the real cards in the way the lessons show.

A: the helmet mixes saturated blue, white, an orange visor and rims, a red stripe, a magenta wall and a violet ledge. That is too many hue families (5.2), and the whites read cream-pink in the lens. B: the sneakers also carry many neon accents on an orange and yellow backdrop. Both exceed the range, but A's pure orange visor against magenta is the more forced combination.
pairs.fix: Reduce the helmet to blue and white with one orange accent. Make the wall and ledge one calm muted colour instead of magenta plus violet.

pairs.difference: B: the marble lion and plinth are a near-neutral cream mass (subject chroma 0.027, far below the real range). In the lens the warm cream marble shades into the green of the grass, and the hero is the least colourful thing on the card. A: the neon ice cream has cyan and orange on teal with pink glow. It is loud but in range.
pairs.fix: Give the lion a clearer local colour, such as warm sandstone or a light golden stone, with cooler blue-grey shadows. That way the statue stands out from the green park instead of fading into cream.

pattern: Generated cards still give themselves away by swapping cool or neutral whites for cream. They also show either a single pure hue on the hero with same-chroma shadows, or shadows that collapse to grey-black. Some go to a one-family palette, like the lavender moon or the grey console. The hero and background chroma are also often mismatched: the subject is too dull or the background is louder than anything on the real cards.
